app.run: Leserina is a static Vite web app (a PWA); it needs nothing but its dev server. Start it in the background on a free port, with its PID and log in your workspace's git dir (gitignored, one per workspace): `d="$(git rev-parse --git-dir)"; node_modules/.bin/vite --host --port 0 > "$d/leserina-dev.log" 2>&1 & echo $! > "$d/leserina-dev.pid"`. Port 0 picks a free port, so several workspaces run side by side; the log's `Local:` line gives the address (http://localhost:<port>/leserina/). It reloads by itself after any change in `src/`, and on every new file in `audio/` or `pictures/`; after a change to `vite.config.ts` or `words.json`, restart it. Only for work on syncing between devices: the sync worker answers only ports 5180/5181, so then start Vite with `--port 5180` instead (if no other workspace holds it) and the worker beside it from `worker/`: `node_modules/.bin/wrangler dev --ip 0.0.0.0 > "$d/leserina-worker.log" 2>&1 & echo $! > "$d/leserina-worker.pid"` (port 8787, local data only, never the families' real data). There is no login. A fresh browser has no children yet: on the start screen, "Elternbereich öffnen" opens the parents' corner, where you add a child under a made-up name (Lena, Max; never real children's names), pick an animal and settings (picture style, "Laute vorsprechen", "Wörter legen"); back on the start screen, tap the child to play a round. Later the parents' corner opens by holding the lock at the bottom right for a moment. Show it at an iPad size (1180×820, landscape) or a phone (393×852). Browser runs must stay silent: stub `speechSynthesis` in the page (Obeya's browser and demo skills do already), because words without a clip are spoken by the system voice. Stop it when done with `kill $(cat "$d/leserina-dev.pid")` (and the worker's PID file likewise); killing the PID takes the child processes along.
app.stop: d="$(git rev-parse --git-dir)"; for f in "$d/leserina-dev.pid" "$d/leserina-worker.pid"; do [ -f "$f" ] && kill "$(cat "$f")" 2>/dev/null; rm -f "$f"; done; true
